question: An architect is about to spawn a new subagent to investigate the caching layer, but suspects a similar investigation may already have been done earlier in the exploration. What should the architect check first to avoid redundant exploration?
options: A) Nothing; spawn the new subagent immediately regardless of what earlier phases may have already found.
B) The user's personal notes taken outside the Claude Code session, since those are the only reliable record of prior work.
C) The main agent's unaided memory of the conversation from several hours ago, trusting it to recall every earlier finding.
D) The manifest or scratchpad records from earlier phases, to see whether the caching layer was already investigated.
correct_answers: D) The manifest or scratchpad records from earlier phases, to see whether the caching layer was already investigated.
explanations: Incorrect. Spawning without checking risks duplicating an investigation that has already been completed, wasting time and tokens.
Incorrect. Personal notes outside the session are not integrated into the agent workflow; the scratchpad and manifest records are the mechanism designed for this purpose.
Incorrect. Relying on the main agent's unaided recall from hours earlier is exactly the kind of context degradation the scratchpad and manifest are meant to counteract.
Correct. Checking the manifest or scratchpad records shows what has already been discovered and recorded, avoiding the cost of spawning a subagent to redo captured work.
